wiki_text: Following completion of the expansion (third 180,000-cbm LNG tank and a second jetty), the President Lech Kaczyński LNG terminal in Świnoujście reached a total regasification capacity of 8.3 bcm/year as of 1 January 2025 (up from 5 bcm in 2015 and 6.2 bcm in 2022). This matches the GEM unit breakdown of 3.7 + 0.9 + 1.5 = 6.1 mtpa (~8.3 bcm/y).

Gaz-System is advancing a second FSRU ('FSRU 2') at the Gulf of Gdańsk terminal that would add ~4.5 bcm/y of regasification capacity. After a 2025 market screening showed demand for 2031-2032 exceeding the planned FSRU 2 capacity nearly fourfold (with almost half of regasified LNG slated for export to Ukraine, Slovakia, Czechia and Lithuania), Gaz-System launched a binding FSRU 2 open season procedure in March 2026; results will underpin a possible final investment decision. Remains pre-FID (proposed).

The Gdańsk FSRU (FSRU 1, ~6.1 bcm/y) is chartered by Gaz-System from a 100%-owned subsidiary of Mitsui O.S.K. Lines (MOL) under a long-term time charter; the vessel will be managed by the MOL group. The 170,000-cbm FSRU (Hull No. 3515, ~295 m x 46 m) is being built at HD Hyundai Heavy Industries in Ulsan, South Korea; it was launched/floated in May 2026, is scheduled to arrive in the Gulf of Gdańsk at end-2027, with regasification services starting Q1 2028. Vessel remains unnamed as of mid-2026.
